findings.title: Unescaped embed URL stored as raw HTML enables stored XSS
findings.body: In app/models/topic_embed.rb line 13 the embed URL is interpolated directly into HTML "#{url}" without escaping. Validation is only url =~ /^https?\:\/\// which only checks the prefix, so a URL like http://example.com/' onmouseover='alert(1) passes. The result is saved with cook_method raw_html and later rendered with raw post.cooked in embed/best.html.erb, so an attacker who controls a feed link or embed URL gets persistent script execution in the embed iframe and topic page.

findings.title: Unescaped request.referer in postMessage allows XSS and breaks resize
findings.body: In app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb line 11 request.referer is interpolated directly into a single-quoted JS string for parent.postMessage. Referer is attacker-controlled via the parent page URL and is not JS-escaped, so a value containing ' or </script> breaks out to execute script. Additionally the second argument to postMessage must be an origin (scheme+host+port) but a full referer URL with path is passed, so browsers reject it and auto-resize never works.

findings.title: Nil feed item content crashes polling job
findings.body: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 35 the code does CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) without checking for nil. RSS/Atom items are not required to have content, and SimpleRSS returns nil for missing fields. A single item without content raises NoMethodError, aborting the whole hourly poll so no feed items are imported.

findings.title: Missing guard on embed_by_username crashes retrieve
findings.body: In lib/topic_retriever.rb line 49 fetch_http does SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase without checking presence. If the setting is blank, nil.downcase raises NoMethodError. Unlike Jobs::PollFeed#execute which guards with present?, every RetrieveTopic job and every embed page miss will crash when the forum has not configured the username.

findings.title: Inverted substring origin check for postMessage
findings.body: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js line 17 the check is discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1. This tests whether the expected URL contains the message origin as a substring instead of testing equality of origins. Any origin that happens to appear as a substring of discourseUrl is accepted, and the logic is backwards from the safe pattern of comparing e.origin to the expected origin, allowing crafted messages to resize the iframe.

findings.title: Check-then-create race violates unique embed_url index
findings.body: In app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 20-28 import does TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first and if blank creates a topic then TopicEmbed.create!. Two concurrent RetrieveTopic jobs for the same URL can both see blank and both insert, so the second hits the unique index on topic_embeds.embed_url and raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, failing the job and potentially leaving a duplicate orphan topic.

findings.title: Non-atomic throttle with setnx+expire can stick forever
findings.body: In lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 27-29 throttling does $redis.setnx then $redis.expire as two separate commands. If the process crashes between them the key is left without a TTL, so that embed_url is throttled forever and never re-fetched. The key also embeds the raw URL unbounded, and should use an atomic SET with NX+EX and a hashed key.

findings.title: Every cache miss triggers full feed poll enabling DoS
findings.body: In lib/topic_retriever.rb line 41 perform_retrieve calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) which fetches and imports the entire RSS feed on every missing embed. Throttling is per-URL (retrieved:#{@embed_url}), so an attacker requesting many distinct paths on the embeddable host bypasses it and forces the server to repeatedly download and process the whole feed, causing load and slow embed responses.

findings.title: Spec tests TopicRetriever path that controller never uses
findings.body: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb the test expects TopicRetriever.new and retrieve when no embed is found, but app/controllers/embed_controller.rb enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic,...) and never calls TopicRetriever directly. The test therefore does not verify real behavior, will fail against the implementation, and leaves the async job enqueue path untested.

findings.title: Disqus import loses original dates and adds remote fetch
findings.body: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor line 148 the import was changed from PostCreator with created_at from the Disqus export to TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link]). import_remote fetches the live URL over HTTP and ignores t[:created_at], so imported topics get current timestamps instead of original dates, imports fail or are slow when links are dead, and the removed category option silently drops categorization.
